title: Implement roleplay engine with memory isolation
description:
Create chatbot/rooms/roleplay.py implementing a roleplay engine with scene-aware persona control and memory isolation. Scene roleplay content must not pollute durable factual memory unless explicitly marked for persistence.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/architecture.md
- chatbot/rooms/__init__.py (created by task b.1)
- chatbot/rooms/room.py (created by task b.1 — Room, RoomType, RoomMemoryPolicy, DEFAULT_ROOM_POLICIES)
- chatbot/rooms/scene.py (created by task b.2 — SceneState, scene lifecycle functions)
- chatbot/db/models.py (updated by task b.3 — Room and Scene model classes)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY chatbot/rooms/roleplay.py. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Create chatbot/rooms/roleplay.py with:
   - Module docstring: 'Roleplay engine with scene-aware persona and memory isolation. Scene content is isolated from durable memory unless explicitly marked for persistence.'

2. A `RoleplayPersona` dataclass with: name (str), description (str), traits (list[str]), voice_style (str, e.g. 'formal', 'casual', 'playful'), backstory (str), scene_goals (list[str], default empty), constraints (list[str], default empty).

3. A `RoleplayEngine` class with:
   - `__init__(self, scene: SceneState, persona: RoleplayPersona)`: stores scene reference and persona. Loads the room's memory_policy from DEFAULT_ROOM_POLICIES unless overridden.
   - `build_scene_prompt(self) -> str`: constructs a system prompt combining persona description, scene context (location, activity, tone, intensity), backstory, and constraints. Includes instruction to stay in character.
   - `classify_memory_importance(self, content: str) -> Literal['scene_only', 'durable', 'both']`: template-based classifier (no LLM) that checks for explicit markers like '[remember this]' or '[important]' to promote scene content to durable memory. Also checks for proper-noun facts and relationship declarations. Otherwise returns 'scene_only'.
   - `generate_scene_context(self) -> str`: returns a compact context string combining scene summary, persona traits, and any scene goals.
   - `is_durable_candidate(self, turn_text: str) -> bool`: returns True if the turn text contains explicit persist markers or classified as 'durable'. Used by the turn pipeline and memory retrieval to decide whether scene content should be written to durable memory.
   - `get_scene_memory_scope(self) -> str`: returns the room's memory_scope value for retrieval filtering.

4. All classification and decision logic is deterministic template-based — no LLM calls.
acceptance_criteria: chatbot/rooms/roleplay.py exists and defines RoleplayPersona, RoleplayEngine
RoleplayPersona has name, description, traits, voice_style, backstory, scene_goals, constraints
RoleplayEngine.build_scene_prompt() returns a system prompt with persona and scene context
RoleplayEngine.classify_memory_importance() returns 'durable' when content contains '[remember this]' or '[important]'
RoleplayEngine.is_durable_candidate() returns False by default, True for explicitly marked content
No LLM provider calls anywhere in the module
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: call LLM providers for classification or generation
change the Abracapocus runtime, orchestrator, or backends

allowed: use Literal for classification return type
use regex or keyword matching for explicit persist markers
access SceneState and RoomMemoryPolicy from sibling room modules
construct system prompts from persona and scene fields via string templates
forbidden: call LLM providers (the classify function must be deterministic)
modify the database directly from this module
introduce LangChain, LangGraph, or any agent framework
hard-code specific persona profiles or characters
